findings.issue_text: [Critical/bug] In credential-sync mode, refreshOAuthTokens returns the raw fetch Response instead of the wrapped return type callers expect: googlecalendar CalendarService reads res?.data (undefined on a Response, so token.access_token throws TypeError), hubspot treats it as a HubspotToken (missing access_token/expires_in fields), zohocrm and zoho-bigin access .data.error (TypeError), and even fetch-based adapters (lark, zoom) receive a differently-shaped body breaking downstream parsers like handleLarkError — the sync path is broken for essentially every adapter.

[High/bug] In parseRefreshTokenResponse, the computed keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] both evaluate to a single constant literal key (e.g. "[object Object]"), not wildcards, so the intended any-property-with-a-number-is-the-expiry logic does not exist; combined with zod's default key-stripping, the parsed data retains only access_token and silently drops the expiry and every other field of the response.

[High/data] parseRefreshTokenResponse injects the literal string "refresh_token" into the data when the parsed data lacks refresh_token (always true in sync mode due to the key-stripping); office365calendar CalendarService spreads this into o365AuthCredentials before prisma.credential.update, overwriting the user's real refresh token with a garbage placeholder and permanently breaking the integration until re-authorization.

[Medium/bug] The lenient schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse is selected purely from env vars rather than whether the sync path was actually taken: with sync enabled, responses obtained directly from providers are also minimally parsed and stripped — e.g. salesforce CalendarService persists a stripped Salesforce token (losing instance_url, signature, etc. that jsforce needs), and team credentials (userId null → local refresh) are corrupted the same way.

[Medium/security] The webhook secret in app-credential.ts is compared with plain !==, a timing-unsafe comparison, on an endpoint that can create/overwrite any user's OAuth credentials; crypto.timingSafeEqual should be used.

[Medium/security] The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret/auth header is sent) and the returned live OAuth access tokens are consumed with no verification at all: no response.ok/status check, no timeout, and an http:// endpoint would exchange tokens in cleartext.

[Medium/bug] zoho-bigin CalendarService passes credentialId as the third (userId) argument to refreshOAuthTokens, so the sync endpoint receives the credential's DB id as calcomUserId (wrong identity mapping; every other adapter correctly passes credential.userId).

[Medium/concurrency] The findFirst-then-create/update sequence in app-credential.ts has a TOCTOU race: two concurrent webhook calls for the same (userId, appId) can both find nothing and both create, producing duplicate credentials; there is no unique constraint or upsert.

[Medium/api] appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body) throws an unhandled ZodError and JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is unprotected, so malformed or undecryptable payloads produce unhandled 500s instead of 400/422 responses.

[Medium/bug] salesforce CalendarService checks if (response.statusText !== "OK"), which is unreliable (statusText varies by server/locale and is empty for HTTP/2 responses) and mislabels upstream failures as 400; response.ok/response.status should be used instead.

[Medium/performance] A Salesforce token refresh (network call) plus a credential DB write now run unconditionally on every service instantiation (i.e. every calendar/booking operation) instead of only when the token is expired as jsforce's lazy refresh previously did — extra Salesforce API traffic, DB write churn, and transient refresh failures now break every operation.

[Medium/test_gap] No tests exist for the new credential-writing webhook (secret verification, decryption, update-vs-create), parseRefreshTokenResponse, or refreshOAuthTokens — high-risk credential paths, several of which contain the logic defects listed above.
[Low/bug] The app-credential webhook handler never checks req.method, so any HTTP method (GET, etc.) is processed and hits body parsing.

[Low/data] The decrypted keys are persisted as credential.key without being validated against the app's credential schema, so a wrong-keyed or malformed payload silently poisons the credential and only fails later at runtime.

[Low/bug] The header name from CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is used without .toLowerCase() even though Node lowercases incoming header keys (a mixed-case value silently rejects valid secrets), and req.headers[...] may be string[], making the strict comparison always fail.

[Low/bug] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED in constants.ts is typed string | undefined (the result of a && b on two env strings), not boolean, despite the _ENABLED name; strict-boolean usage will silently misbehave.

[Low/bug] Regression in office365calendar: the previous code logged the zod error plus the provider response and continued after a failed token parse; parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", removing diagnostic context and turning previously non-fatal parse failures into hard failures.

goldens.comment: The parseRefreshTokenResponse function incorrectly sets refresh_token to the hardcoded string 'refresh_token' when it's missing from the OAuth refresh token response. This invalidates the token, breaking subsequent token refreshes and causing authentication failures.

The Zod schema in parseRefreshTokenResponse uses computed property keys [z.string().toString()] and [z.string().optional().toString()] in minimumTokenResponseSchema, which is invalid Zod syntax and will throw a runtime error.

parseRefreshTokenResponse returns a Zod safeParse result ({ success, data, error }), not the credential key object. Persisting that as key stores the wrapper instead of the token payload; we should store the parsed data or use schema parse.

When APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED and CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT are set, the refreshFunction helper returns the fetch Response, but several callers (for example GoogleCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting res.data, and HubspotCalendarService.refreshAccessToken expecting a HubspotToken) assume it returns the integration-specific token object. That mismatch will cause runtime errors in the sync-enabled path unless the return type or those call sites are adjusted.

When the sync endpoint path is used, res is a fetch Response and has no .data; res?.data will be undefined and token.access_token will throw at runtime. This relies on a consistent return shape from refreshOAuthTokens, which isn’t guaranteed currently.

The `refreshOAuthTokens` function is passed `credentialId` instead of `userId`, which breaks the credential sync functionality by causing incorrect user lookups. This issue can lead to failures in syncing user credentials, impacting user experience.

The Salesforce integration checks `response.statusText` instead of `response.ok` when handling OAuth token refresh responses. This can lead to unreliable behavior, as a successful response may not be correctly identified, resulting in the use of stale credentials and potential authentication failures.

The `jsforce.Connection` is created using stale `credentialKey.access_token` and `credentialKey.instance_url` after a token refresh, which can lead to authentication failures and incorrect data access. Ensure that the connection is established using the refreshed token values instead.

The `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse` function can throw on invalid payloads, resulting in 500 Internal Server Errors instead of the expected 400 Bad Request responses. This can lead to confusion for clients and hinder proper error handling.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, `minimumTokenResponseSchema` uses computed keys `[z.string().toString()]` and `[z.string().optional().toString()]` inside `z.object({...})`. Those expressions evaluate immediately to a single literal string key (e.g. `"[object Object]"` or similar), not a wildcard/pattern for arbitrary properties. As a result, the schema does not implement the intended "any numeric property is expiry" behavior and will either (a) fail parsing because the response won't contain that exact literal key, or (b) if it did parse, Zod's object schema would strip unknown keys, losing fields like `expiry_date`. This is a concrete correctness issue introduced by the new file.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the choice of schema is based only on `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`, not on whether `refreshOAuthTokens` actually used the sync endpoint. This means that when those env vars are set, *all* refresh responses (including direct provider refreshes taken when `userId` is null/absent, e.g. team credentials) are validated/parsed with `minimumTokenResponseSchema` instead of the provider-specific schema passed in. Since Zod objects strip unknown keys by default, this can drop provider-required fields. The diff shows Salesforce now persists refreshed tokens via `parseRefreshTokenResponse(accessTokenJson, salesforceTokenSchema)` and then updates `credential.key` from `accessTokenParsed.data`; with envs set, the minimal schema would be used and could omit fields like `instance_url`/`signature` that `jsforce.Connection` typically relies on, matching the finding’s data-loss/corruption concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] The webhook secret in app-credential.ts is compared with plain !==, a timing-unsafe comparison, on an endpoint that can create/overwrite any user's OAuth credentials; crypto.timingSafeEqual should be used.

adjudication.rationale:
In the newly added endpoint `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the webhook secret check is implemented as a direct inequality comparison:
```ts
if (req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET)
```
This is a timing-unsafe string comparison. Given this endpoint can `prisma.credential.update` / `create` credentials for an arbitrary `userId` provided in the request body (after passing only this shared-secret check), the secret comparison is the primary gate and should avoid timing side-channels (e.g., `crypto.timingSafeEqual` on normalized `Buffer`s with length checks).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/security] The POST to CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT carries no authentication (no secret/auth header is sent) and the returned live OAuth access tokens are consumed with no verification at all: no response.ok/status check, no timeout, and an http:// endpoint would exchange tokens in cleartext.

adjudication.rationale: The new `refreshOAuthTokens` helper (packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/refreshOAuthTokens.ts) sends a POST to `process.env.CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT` with only a URL-encoded body (`calcomUserId`, `appSlug`) and no authentication/secret header. It also returns the raw `fetch(...)` response without checking `response.ok`/status or enforcing HTTPS/timeout. Call sites then consume the response as if it were valid token data (e.g., GoogleCalendarService reads `res?.data` and proceeds to set `access_token`/`expiry_date`), meaning an unauthenticated/unchecked endpoint (including `http://`) could supply/alter live OAuth tokens.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the handler does a non-atomic `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { userId, appId } })` followed by either `prisma.credential.create(...)` or `prisma.credential.update(...)`. This check-then-act sequence is vulnerable to concurrent requests for the same `(userId, appId)` both seeing no existing row and both attempting `create`, which can result in duplicate credentials if no DB uniqueness exists, or a thrown unique-constraint error if it does. The diff shows no `upsert`/transaction/locking or unique-violation handling in this code path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/performance] A Salesforce token refresh (network call) plus a credential DB write now run unconditionally on every service instantiation (i.e. every calendar/booking operation) instead of only when the token is expired as jsforce's lazy refresh previously did — extra Salesforce API traffic, DB write churn, and transient refresh failures now break every operation.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the diff adds an unconditional refresh-token network request (`fetch("https://login.salesforce.com/services/oauth2/token", ...)`) and a subsequent `prisma.credential.update(...)` immediately after `const credentialKey = ...` and before returning `new jsforce.Connection(...)`. There is no expiry/need check in the shown code path, so every time this connection-creation logic runs it will perform the refresh call + DB write, which can create extra Salesforce API traffic and DB churn and makes operations more sensitive to transient refresh failures. The claim about jsforce's prior lazy-refresh behavior isn't verifiable from this diff, but the new unconditional behavior is.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/test_gap] No tests exist for the new credential-writing webhook (secret verification, decryption, update-vs-create), parseRefreshTokenResponse, or refreshOAuthTokens — high-risk credential paths, several of which contain the logic defects listed above.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds several new, high-impact code paths (a new credential-writing webhook at apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts, plus new OAuth helpers packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts and refreshOAuthTokens.ts) but the diff contains no corresponding test additions (no new/modified test files or assertions covering secret verification, decryption/JSON parse, update-vs-create branching, or the conditional schema/endpoint behavior). This is a specific, diff-grounded gap for newly introduced credential-handling logic, but not itself a direct functional defect proven by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] The app-credential webhook handler never checks req.method, so any HTTP method (GET, etc.) is processed and hits body parsing.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the `handler` processes requests without checking `req.method`. It unconditionally runs `appCredentialWebhookRequestBodySchema.parse(req.body)`, so a GET/PUT/etc. request (likely with an empty/nonconforming body) will throw a Zod exception and result in a 500 rather than returning a proper 405/400. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior issue in the new handler.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/data] The decrypted keys are persisted as credential.key without being validated against the app's credential schema, so a wrong-keyed or malformed payload silently poisons the credential and only fails later at runtime.

adjudication.rationale: In the new webhook handler `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the payload `reqBody.keys` is decrypted and `JSON.parse`d into `keys`, then written directly to `prisma.credential.update/create` as `data: { key: keys }` without any validation against an app-specific credential schema (only `appStoreMetadata` is consulted for `slug`/`type`). This allows malformed or wrong-shaped data to be persisted and potentially break later consumers at runtime.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] The header name from CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME is used without .toLowerCase() even though Node lowercases incoming header keys (a mixed-case value silently rejects valid secrets), and req.headers[...] may be string[], making the strict comparison always fail.

adjudication.rationale: In the new API route `apps/web/pages/api/webhook/app-credential.ts`, the secret check uses `req.headers[process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME || "calcom-webhook-secret"] !== process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET`. `req.headers` (Node/Next `IncomingHttpHeaders`) normalizes header *keys* to lowercase, so if `CALCOM_WEBHOOK_HEADER_NAME` is set to any mixed-case value, the lookup will miss and reject valid requests. Additionally, `req.headers[...]` is typed as `string | string[] | undefined`; if the header is provided multiple times and becomes a `string[]`, the strict string comparison will always fail, also rejecting valid secrets. Both issues are directly verifiable from the diff and affect correctness of webhook authentication.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED in constants.ts is typed string | undefined (the result of a && b on two env strings), not boolean, despite the _ENABLED name; strict-boolean usage will silently misbehave.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/lib/constants.ts`, `APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED` is defined as `process.env.CALCOM_WEBHOOK_SECRET && process.env.CALCOM_APP_CREDENTIAL_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, which evaluates to a `string | undefined` (the second env value) rather than a boolean. While the diff only uses it in truthiness checks (e.g., `if (!APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED)` and `if (APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && ...)`) where it behaves as intended, the `_ENABLED` name strongly implies a boolean flag and the non-boolean type can be misleading and error-prone for future/other usages (e.g., strict boolean expectations or comparisons). Coercing via `!!(...)` would align type/semantics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] Regression in office365calendar: the previous code logged the zod error plus the provider response and continued after a failed token parse; parseRefreshTokenResponse now throws a generic "Invalid refreshed tokens were returned", removing diagnostic context and turning previously non-fatal parse failures into hard failures.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the previous logic did `refreshTokenResponseSchema.safeParse(responseJson)`, logged `tokenResponse.error` and `responseJson` on failure, and then continued (updating credentials with the unmodified `o365AuthCredentials`). The new code uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`, which throws `new Error("Invalid refreshed tokens were returned")` when parsing fails and no longer logs the provider response/error context. This is a real behavior/diagnostics change visible in the diff, though whether throwing is "wrong" is not provable as a correctness defect from the diff alone.
